the QuEChERS technique is the method of choice for the analysis of plant material.
the QuEChERS technique, in combination with GC-MS/MS, is an excellent choice for the analysis of the selected pesticides in plant matrices.
the extraction of pesticides from plants is still a challenge for analytical chemists, and there is no single extraction method that would be the best solution in all the cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the extraction of neonicotinoidal, pyrethoidal and sulfonyluric pesticides from plant matrix can be performed with the highest effectiveness by the application of QuEChERS method, while for phenylamidic compounds the best results are achieved when the extraction is performed in the mixture of methanol and water.

there is still much space for further research on the optimization of extraction techniques for pesticides from plant tissues, especially for the new sorbent materials and the new extraction techniques.
QuEChERS is a universal extraction method, which is suitable for the extraction of pesticides from plant materials, but it is not the best solution for all analytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most promising techniques in the future will be the ones that will combine the advantages of both liquid and solid extraction techniques, such as pressurized liquid extraction and QuEChERS.
the extraction technique should be chosen based on the analyte class.
